subject: Calyx private cluster: provisioning, network encryption, and IO SLA
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@calyxsystems.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@calyxsystems.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Calyx: private deployment — initial requirements and clarifying questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We dug into internal requirements and wanted to put everything on paper so your team can propose a concrete footprint. High-level asks from our infra and security teams: 

- Dedicated on-prem Kubernetes cluster running inside our DMZ-connected data center (no public outbound to vendor-controlled endpoints).
- VPC-equivalent networking with static egress controls; BGP to our edge routers preferred.
- All model artifact storage must be encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (we use HashiCorp Vault; HSM accessible in lane A).
- Node-level isolation: GPU pools for inference, separate node pool for control-plane sidecars and telemetry; ephemeral worker node pool for batch jobs.
- Minimum IO SLA: 10,000 IOPS sustained for inference tier with 99.9% availability window for attachments/weights.

Can you confirm what node types you recommend, an initial node count for an MVP serving 25 req/s p50 latency ~75ms, and whether Redwood supports an air-gapped deployment profile? I attached our internal network diagram and a rough traffic profile.

Attachments: calyx_network_diagram_v2.pdf, mvp_node_sizing.csv

Best,
Alex Garcia
Head of Infrastructure — Calyx Systems
alex.garcia@calyxsystems.com
+1 (415) 555-0124
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@calyxsystems.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx: private deployment — initial requirements and clarifying questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list and diagrams. High level responses below; Neha and Irene are looped for sizing and networking specifics. Quick summary up front:

- Yes, we can support a private, customer-controlled on-prem deployment with no vendor egress. We provide an air-gap-friendly package and a VPC-equivalent network model.
- For customer-managed KMS/HSM integration: we support Vault-derived CMKs via our KMS adapter; will need service account token exchange and short-lived certs for the control plane.
- Recommended starting node mix (MVP): 3 control-plane nodes (no GPUs), 4 inference nodes (2x A100-class or equivalent), 2 batch/rollback worker nodes. This matches the 25 req/s target with expected burst headroom.

Neha — can you produce a quick sensitivity table (IO and CPU) for 25/50/100 req/s and the expected pod densities? Irene — can you sketch the network egress model (BGP peering + static NAT) and a fallback when BGP is unavailable?

I attached the mutual action plan template (RITM-1729_mutual_action_plan.xlsx) to start tasks and owners.

Thanks — Markus

Markus Klein
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@calyxsystems.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx: private deployment — initial requirements and clarifying questions

Hi all,

Quick sizing table attached inside — pasted the most relevant rows below for convenience. My assumptions: token sizes typical for our catalog model (~50 tokens avg), KV cache enabled with a 30s TTL for sessions, and parallelism limited to 4 concurrent streams per GPU for latency targets.

MVP target (25 req/s):
- Inference nodes: 4x GPU nodes (each 1 GPU, 80GB VRAM class) => estimates 28–32 streams aggregate; typical p50 ~= 70ms, p95 ~= 240ms under steady state.
- Storage: weights on encrypted NVMe (local), model checkpoint archive on encrypted network blockstore (replicated).
- IO profile: 10–12k sustained IOPS per inference node during warmup; recommended baseline 40k IOPS for the inference tier.

Scaling notes (50 req/s): +4 inference nodes; consider per-node cache warmup automation. For 100 req/s choose 12 inference nodes and introduce an L2 local SSD cache tier to lower blockstore IOPS.

Action items:
- Calyx: confirm total on-site rack space (RU) and whether you can provide KMS access via an internal transit gateway.
- Redwood: we will produce a per-node cost estimate and the deployment manifest for an air-gapped install.

-neha

Attachments referenced: mvp_node_sizing.csv
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@calyxsystems.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@calyxsystems.com>
Date: 2026-10-24T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx: private deployment — initial requirements and clarifying questions

Thanks Mark, Neha — this is exactly the level we needed. A few clarifications from our security team after reviewing your notes: 

1) Vault integration: we can provide an AppRole with constrained permissions; however our policy requires all external control-plane requests to be proxied through an internal service account boundary. Is Redwood able to accept short-lived certs minted by a Calyx-side CA?
2) Air-gap: we will need a documented procedure for offline model updates (we prefer bundle-based shipping). Can your team produce an offline bundle signer and verify tooling?
3) IO SLA: the 40k IOPS baseline is doable, but we need an agreement on how Redwood will measure compliance (metrics, sampling windows, and remediation steps).

I attached an updated network diagram showing where KMS transit would terminate. If this looks feasible I'd like to schedule a follow-up deep-dive Thursday.

-Alex

On Thu, Oct 22, 2026 at 09:17 AM Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@calyxsystems.com> wrote:
> [original message clipped]
From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-26T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx: private deployment — initial requirements and clarifying questions

Alex — quick notes ahead of Thursday's call so we can hit the action items: 

- KMS/CAs: Redwood supports Calyx-minted short-lived certs for the control plane; we will require a one-time exchange of the CA root and an automated renewal hook. We'll document the exact CSR flow and provide an Ansible role to place certs in the control plane.
- Offline bundles: we have an 'airgap-bundle' tool that signs bundles with an operator key; we can run signing in your environment or provide an offline signer binary and verification utility. We'll include checksum verification and manifest signatures.
- IO measurement: propose an acceptance window of 24h for initial provisioning, sampling p95 and p99 IOPS with a 15-minute sliding window; remediation: temporary burst capacity and node replacement within SLA if persistent under-provisioning is observed.

Please confirm available times for Thursday; I'll prepare a network peering diagram (BGP + static NAT fallback) and a proposal for an L2 SSD cache tier if Calyx wants to reduce blockstore pressure.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
(end of thread)
